purpose: Compare a model with a forecast while preserving direction and support conditions.
meaning: Relative entropy compares distributions in a specified direction using their probability-weighted log ratio. It is nonnegative, zero exactly when they agree, generally asymmetric, and infinite if Q excludes an outcome with positive P probability. Individual contributions can be negative.

definition.setting: A teaching model gives sticker probability p. A forecast uses q. Compare the Bernoulli distributions P=(1−p,p) and Q=(1−q,q), keeping the direction P∥Q explicit.

signature.p: Sticker chance in teaching model P.
signature.D(P∥Q): Relative entropy from P to Q in bits.

prompts.prompt: How much relative entropy separates P=(1/4,3/4) from Q=(1/2,1/2)?
prompts.answer: Contributions are (1/4)log₂(1/2)=−1/4 and (3/4)log₂(3/2). They sum to approximately 0.188722 bits. A negative individual term is allowed; the full divergence is nonnegative.
